title: Quasi-identifier combining in sensor events
description: Motion/door/sensor events combined with timestamps and location data can create quasi-identifiers that link data to specific individuals or their routines
assumptions: Events contain multiple attributes that can be combined to identify individuals

title: Revealing attributes in event data
description: The nature of events (motion, door open/close, sensor triggers) reveals information about occupants' presence, activities, and routines
assumptions: Event types and timestamps reveal behavioral patterns about data subjects

title: Potentially sensitive data types collected
description: Motion and door events may be more sensitive than functionally required for basic home automation functionality
assumptions: Some sensor data could be perceived as highly sensitive by occupants

title: Excessive data retention in event log
description: Event log may store sensor data longer than functionally needed for the home hub's operation
assumptions: No clear retention policy or automatic deletion mechanism

title: Unawareness of event logging
description: Occupants may not be aware that their motion/door/sensor events are being logged and stored
assumptions: No clear notification or consent mechanism for data collection

title: Lack of data subject control over preferences
description: Occupants have no control over what sensor data is collected, how it's processed, or how long it's retained
assumptions: No user interface or settings for data collection preferences

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing more personal data than actually needed for the functional goals of the home hub
assumptions: All sensor events are collected regardless of functional necessity

title: Linking through unique identifiers in video metadata
description: Video clips uploaded to cloud storage may contain metadata with unique identifiers (timestamps, device IDs, user accounts) that can link the video content to specific individuals or households.
assumptions: Video metadata includes identifying information

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combination
description: Combination of video content attributes (location, time, visual features) with metadata can serve as quasi-identifiers to link data to specific individuals.
assumptions: Video content combined with metadata creates linkable attributes

title: Revealing attributes in video content
description: Video clips contain revealing attributes (faces, activities, locations, behaviors) that support identification of data subjects.
assumptions: Video surveillance captures identifiable personal information

title: Small anonymity set allows singling out
description: In home surveillance context, the anonymity set is small (typically one household), allowing individuals to be singled out from video content.
assumptions: Home surveillance targets specific individuals with limited anonymity

title: Highly sensitive video data type collected
description: Video footage is highly sensitive personal data that should only be collected when strictly required for the system's functional purpose.
assumptions: Video is more sensitive than minimally necessary for home security

title: Excessive volume of video data processed
description: Continuous or frequent recording of video clips may process excessive amounts of personal data beyond functional necessity.
assumptions: Video recording may be continuous or frequent

title: Data propagation to cloud services
description: Video data is propagated to cloud storage services where it may be accessible by parties beyond the immediate functional need.
assumptions: Cloud storage involves third-party service providers

title: Predetermined set of cloud service parties
description: Video data is made accessible to predetermined cloud storage service providers, expanding exposure beyond immediate users.
assumptions: Cloud storage involves known third-party providers

title: Unawareness of video processing by data subjects
description: Data subjects may not be fully aware of the extent of video collection, processing, and storage occurring in their home environment.
assumptions: Users may not understand full data processing implications

title: Limited control over video data processing preferences
description: Data subjects may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how video data is processed, stored, and shared.
assumptions: Limited user control mechanisms for video data

title: Difficulty rectifying or erasing video data
description: Data subjects may lack control to rectify incorrect video data or remove personal data that is no longer relevant.
assumptions: Video deletion/rectification may be difficult or limited

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Video data collection may process more personal data than actually needed for the stated functional purpose of home security.
assumptions: GDPR data minimization principle applies

title: Violation of storage limitation principle
description: Video data may be stored longer than functionally needed, violating storage limitation requirements.
assumptions: Extended video retention periods may occur

title: Linking through unique identifier in motion alert
description: The real-time motion alert may contain device identifiers or user identifiers that could be used to link data to specific individuals across systems.
assumptions: Motion alerts include device/user identifiers

title: Quasi-identifier combining in motion data
description: Motion data combined with other attributes (time, location, device type) could serve as quasi-identifiers to link data to individuals.
assumptions: Motion alerts contain multiple attributes that can be combined

title: Processing of identified data in motion alerts
description: The motion alert may contain identified information about the user or device that is being processed and forwarded.
assumptions: Motion alerts contain user-identifying information

title: Revealing attributes in motion data
description: Motion data may reveal revealing attributes such as location, time of activity, or behavioral patterns that support identification of the data subject.
assumptions: Motion data contains revealing attributes

title: Data type sensitivity - motion data may be more sensitive than needed
description: Motion data could be perceived as highly sensitive and may be collected/processed beyond what is functionally required for the alert functionality.
assumptions: Motion data is more sensitive than the alert functionality requires

title: Data propagation to unnecessary services
description: Motion alert data may be propagated to the mobile app backend where it may not be strictly needed for the core alert functionality.
assumptions: Data is shared beyond functional necessity

title: Unawareness of motion data processing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their motion data is being collected, processed, and forwarded to the mobile app backend.
assumptions: Users are not informed about motion data processing

title: Lack of control over motion data preferences
description: Data subjects may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their motion data is processed and shared.
assumptions: No granular consent controls for motion data

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal data (motion data) may be processed than is actually needed for the functional goal of forwarding a motion alert.
assumptions: Motion data collection exceeds functional necessity

title: Processing of identified video data
description: The mobile app backend retrieves stored video clips that are associated with specific homeowners, meaning identified personal data is being processed.
assumptions: Video clips are linked to specific homeowner accounts

title: Revealing attributes in video content
description: Video content may reveal personal attributes about the homeowner (e.g., location, activities, possessions) that support identification of the data subject.
assumptions: Video content captures identifiable information about the homeowner's environment and activities

title: Sensitive video data type collected
description: Video data is highly sensitive personal data that may be collected and processed beyond what is strictly required for playback functionality.
assumptions: Video content contains more sensitive information than necessary for simple playback

title: Potential unnecessary video processing
description: Video data may be further treated, analyzed, or enriched beyond what is needed for the playback functionality (e.g., metadata extraction, content analysis).
assumptions: System may perform additional processing on video data beyond simple retrieval and playback
uncertainty_note: Depends on actual system implementation - assuming potential for additional processing

title: Homeowner unawareness of video processing
description: The homeowner (data subject) may not be fully aware of how their video data is being collected, stored, processed, or potentially disclosed by the system.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain all processing activities related to video data

title: Lack of homeowner control over video processing
description: The homeowner may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their video data is processed, stored, or shared.
assumptions: Limited user controls for video data management settings

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Video data processing may exceed what is actually needed for the stated functionality of retrieving and playing back video clips.
assumptions: System may process more video data than functionally required
uncertainty_note: Depends on actual system design and data minimization practices

title: Video data accessible to multiple parties
description: Video data retrieved by the mobile app backend may be accessible to more parties than functionally necessary (e.g., backend services, third-party integrations).
assumptions: Video data may be propagated to other services or systems beyond the immediate playback need
